translations.idiomatic: The Xuanhui commissioner reported: "The rite is complete.

sentences.zh: 」導歸幄次。

translations.literal: He led her back to the tent-side quarters.
translations.idiomatic: He led her back to the tent-side quarters.

sentences.zh: 宣徽使奏：「請解身體。

translations.literal: The Xuanhui commissioner memorialized: "I request that the ceremonial attire be removed.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuanhui commissioner reported: "I request that the ceremonial attire be removed.

sentences.zh: 嚴。

translations.literal: Strict silence is lifted.
translations.idiomatic: Strict silence is lifted.

sentences.zh: 」內外命婦還幕次。

translations.literal: The inner and outer titled ladies returned to their curtain-side quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The inner and outer titled ladies returned to their curtain-side quarters.

sentences.zh: 少頃，轉仗還內如來儀，外命婦退。

translations.literal: After a short while the guard of honor was redeployed for the return to the palace as on the outward journey, and the outer titled ladies withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: After a short while the guard of honor was redeployed for the return to the palace as on the way in, and the outer titled ladies withdrew.

sentences.zh: 內侍奏：「請禦輿。

translations.literal: A palace attendant memorialized: "I request that Your Majesty take the palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: A palace attendant reported: "I request that Your Majesty take the palanquin.

sentences.zh: 」出至車所，奏：「請升車。

translations.literal: She went out to the carriage station, and he memorialized: "I request that Your Majesty ascend the carriage.
translations.idiomatic: She went out to the carriage station, and he reported: "I request that Your Majesty ascend the carriage.

sentences.zh: 」既升車，奏：「請進發。

translations.literal: Once she had ascended the carriage, he memorialized: "I request that the procession depart.
translations.idiomatic: Once she had ascended the carriage, he reported: "I request that the procession depart.

sentences.zh: 」內命婦上車。

translations.literal: The inner titled ladies mounted their carriages.
translations.idiomatic: The inner titled ladies mounted their carriages.

sentences.zh: 至元德東偏門，內侍奏：「請降車升輿。

translations.literal: Reaching the east side gate of Yuande, a palace attendant memorialized: "I request that Your Majesty descend from the carriage and ascend the palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: At the east side gate of Yuande, a palace attendant reported: "I request that Your Majesty descend from the carriage and ascend the palanquin.

sentences.zh: 」後禦輿，取便路還內，內命婦從入。

translations.literal: Thereafter she took the palanquin and returned to the palace by the convenient route; the inner titled ladies followed her in.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter she took the palanquin and returned to the palace by the direct route, and the inner titled ladies followed her in.

sentences.zh: 冊禮畢，百官上表稱賀，並以箋賀中宮。

translations.literal: When the investiture rite was finished, the officials submitted memorials of congratulation, and all likewise sent congratulatory letters to the empress's palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the investiture rite was finished, officials submitted memorials of congratulation, and all likewise sent congratulatory letters to the empress's palace.

sentences.zh: 皇太子恭謝儀

translations.literal: Rite of the Crown Prince's Reverent Thanksgiving
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince's Rite of Reverent Thanksgiving

sentences.zh: 其日質明，東宮應從官各服朝服，所司陳鹵簿金輅于左掖門外。

translations.literal: On that day at dawn, the Eastern Palace attendants who were to accompany him each wore court dress; the responsible officials set out the guard of honor and golden chariot outside the Left Side Gate.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn that day, the Eastern Palace attendants who were to accompany him wore court dress, and the responsible officials set out the guard of honor and golden chariot outside the Left Side Gate.

sentences.zh: 皇太子服遠遊冠、硃明衣，升輿以出，至金輅所，降輿升輅。

translations.literal: The crown prince wore the distant-travel crown and vermilion bright robe, ascended the palanquin and went out, and when he reached the golden chariot he descended from the palanquin and ascended the chariot.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince wore the distant-travel crown and vermilion bright robe, went out on the palanquin, and when he reached the golden chariot he descended from the palanquin and ascended the chariot.

sentences.zh: 左庶子已下夾侍。

translations.literal: The Left Guardian of the Heir and all those below him attended on either side.
translations.idiomatic: The Left Guardian of the Heir and all those below him attended on either side.

sentences.zh: 三帥、三少乘馬導從，餘官亦皆乘馬以從。

translations.literal: The Three Tutors and Three Junior Tutors rode horses to lead and follow, and the remaining officials likewise all mounted horses to follow.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Tutors and Three Junior Tutors rode ahead and behind on horseback, and the remaining officials likewise all mounted and followed.

sentences.zh: 東行，由太廟西階轉至廟，不鳴鐃吹。

translations.literal: They went east, turned by the west steps of the Grand Ancestral Temple to reach the temple, and did not sound the nao and pipes.
translations.idiomatic: They went east, turned by the west steps of the Grand Ancestral Temple to reach the temple, without sounding the nao and pipes.

sentences.zh: 至廟西偏門外降輅步進，由東偏門入幄次，改服袞冕。

translations.literal: Outside the west side gate of the temple he descended from the chariot and walked forward; he entered the tent-side quarters through the east side gate and changed into the robe and cap of state.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the west side gate of the temple he descended from the chariot and walked forward, entered the tent-side quarters through the east side gate, and changed into the robe and cap of state.

sentences.zh: 出次，執圭自南神東偏門入，宮官並太常寺官皆從。

translations.literal: Leaving the side quarters, he took the scepter and entered through the east side gate of the south spirit gate; palace officials and all officials of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices followed.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving the side quarters, he took the scepter and entered through the east side gate of the south spirit gate, followed by palace officials and all officials of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 皇太子入詣殿庭東階之東，西向立，典儀贊：「再拜。

translations.literal: The crown prince entered, went to the east of the east steps of the temple court, and stood facing west; the master of ceremonial intoned: "Bow twice.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince entered, went to the east of the east steps of the temple court, and stood facing west. The master of ceremonial announced: "Bow twice.

sentences.zh: 」訖，升自西階，詣始祖神位前北向，再拜，訖，以次詣逐室行禮，並如上儀。

translations.literal: When that was finished, he ascended by the west steps, went before the founding ancestor's spirit seat facing north, and bowed twice; when that was finished, he proceeded in order to each chamber to perform the rite, all according to the rite above.
translations.idiomatic: When that was finished, he ascended by the west steps, went before the founding ancestor's spirit seat facing north, and bowed twice; then he proceeded in order to each chamber to perform the rite, following the same procedure throughout.

sentences.zh: 訖，降自西階，複西向位俟，典儀稱：「禮畢。

translations.literal: When that was finished, he descended by the west steps, returned to the west-facing position, and waited; the master of ceremonial called out: "The rite is complete.
translations.idiomatic: When that was finished, he descended by the west steps, returned to the west-facing position, and waited. The master of ceremonial called out: "The rite is complete.

sentences.zh: 」出東神北偏門，謁別廟如上儀。

translations.literal: He went out through the north side gate of the east spirit gate and paid court at the separate temples according to the rite above.
translations.idiomatic: He went out through the north side gate of the east spirit gate and paid court at the separate temples following the same rite.

sentences.zh: 訖，歸幄次，改服遠遊冠、硃明衣。

translations.literal: When that was finished, he returned to the tent-side quarters and changed into the distant-travel crown and vermilion bright robe.
translations.idiomatic: When that was finished, he returned to the tent-side quarters and changed back into the distant-travel crown and vermilion bright robe.

sentences.zh: 出次，步至廟門外升輅，過廟門鳴鐃而行。

translations.literal: Leaving the side quarters, he walked to outside the temple gate and ascended the chariot; once past the temple gate the nao sounded and the procession moved on.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving the side quarters, he walked to outside the temple gate and ascended the chariot; once past the temple gate the nao sounded and the procession set out.

sentences.zh: 至左掖門外降輅，升輿以入。

translations.literal: Outside the Left Side Gate he descended from the chariot and ascended the palanquin to enter.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the Left Side Gate he descended from the chariot, ascended the palanquin, and entered.

sentences.zh: 將士各還本所。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers each returned to their posts.
translations.idiomatic: The officers and soldiers each returned to their posts.

sentences.zh: 後一日於東宮受群官賀，如元正受賀之儀。

translations.literal: On the following day he received congratulations from the assembled officials at the Eastern Palace, according to the rite of receiving congratulations on New Year's Day.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he received congratulations from the assembled officials at the Eastern Palace, following the New Year's Day congratulatory rite.

sentences.zh: 天德二年，命有司議薦新禮，依典禮合用時物，令太常卿行禮。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tiande, the court ordered the responsible officials to deliberate on the rite of seasonal new offerings, to use the seasonal produce appropriate to canonical ritual, and to have the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiande 2, the court ordered the responsible officials to deliberate on the rite of seasonal new offerings, to use the seasonal produce prescribed by canonical ritual, and to have the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices perform the rite.

sentences.zh: 正月，鮪，明昌間用牛魚，無則鯉代。

translations.literal: First month: sturgeon; during the Mingchang period ox-fish was used, and if unavailable carp served as substitute.
translations.idiomatic: First month: sturgeon; during the Mingchang period ox-fish was used, with carp as substitute when unavailable.

sentences.zh: 二月，雁。

translations.literal: Second month: wild geese.
translations.idiomatic: Second month: wild geese.

sentences.zh: 三月，韭，以卵、以葑。

translations.literal: Third month: leeks, with eggs and turnip greens as supplementary offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Third month: leeks, with eggs and turnip greens as supplementary offerings.

sentences.zh: 四月，薦冰。

translations.literal: Fourth month: present ice.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth month: present ice.

sentences.zh: 五月，荀、蒲，羞以含桃。

translations.literal: Fifth month: dogwood and cattail, with cherries as supplementary offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth month: dogwood and cattail, with cherries as supplementary offerings.

sentences.zh: 六月，彘肉、小麥仁。

translations.literal: Sixth month: pork and hulled wheat.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth month: pork and hulled wheat.

sentences.zh: 七月，嘗雛雞以黍，羞以瓜。

translations.literal: Seventh month: taste young chicken with millet, with melons as supplementary offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month: taste young chicken with millet, with melons as supplementary offerings.

sentences.zh: 八月，羞以芡、以菱、以栗。

translations.literal: Eighth month: supplementary offerings of fox nuts, water caltrop, and chestnuts.
translations.idiomatic: Eighth month: supplementary offerings of fox nuts, water caltrop, and chestnuts.

sentences.zh: 九月，嘗粟與稷，羞以棗、以梨。

translations.literal: Ninth month: taste millet and proso millet, with jujubes and pears as supplementary offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Ninth month: taste millet and proso millet, with jujubes and pears as supplementary offerings.

sentences.zh: 十月，嘗麻與稻，羞以兔。

translations.literal: Tenth month: taste hemp seed and rice, with rabbit as supplementary offering.
translations.idiomatic: Tenth month: taste hemp seed and rice, with rabbit as supplementary offering.

sentences.zh: 十一月，羞以麕。

translations.literal: Eleventh month: supplementary offering of muntjac.
translations.idiomatic: Eleventh month: supplementary offering of muntjac.

sentences.zh: 十二月，羞以魚。

translations.literal: Twelfth month: supplementary offering of fish.
translations.idiomatic: Twelfth month: supplementary offering of fish.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 大定三年，有司言：「每歲太廟五享，若複薦新，似涉繁數。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dading, the responsible officials memorialized: "Each year the Grand Ancestral Temple holds five seasonal offerings; if seasonal new offerings are added as well, the number of sacrifices seems excessive.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 3, the responsible officials memorialized: "Each year the Grand Ancestral Temple holds five seasonal offerings; adding seasonal new offerings as well seems excessively frequent.

sentences.zh: 擬遇時享之月，以所薦物附於籩豆薦之，以合古者'祭不欲數'之義。

translations.literal: It is proposed that in months when seasonal offerings are held, the newly offered produce be appended to the baskets and stands of offerings, in accord with the ancient principle that 'sacrifices should not be too frequent.'
translations.idiomatic: They proposed that in months when seasonal offerings were held, the newly offered produce be appended to the baskets and stands of offerings, in accord with the ancient principle that sacrifices should not be too frequent.

sentences.zh: 」制可。

translations.literal: The imperial decree approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial decree approved it.

sentences.zh: 牛魚狀似鮪，鮪之類也。

translations.literal: Ox-fish in shape resembles sturgeon; it is a kind of sturgeon.
translations.idiomatic: Ox-fish resembles sturgeon in shape; it is a kind of sturgeon.

sentences.zh: 功臣配享

translations.literal: Worthy Officials Enshrined in Attendance
translations.idiomatic: Worthy Officials Enshrined in Attendance

sentences.zh: 明昌五年閏十月丙寅，以儀同三司代國公歡都、銀青光祿大夫冶訶、特進劾者、開府儀同三司盆納、儀同三司拔達，配享世祖廟庭。

translations.literal: On bingyin day in the intercalary tenth month of the fifth year of Mingchang, Huandu, Duke of Dai and Grand Master of the State with Unequalled Honor; Yehe, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and Purple Ribbon; Hezhe, Special Advancement; Penna, Grand Master of the State with Unequalled Honor; and Bada, Grand Master of the State with Unequalled Honor, were enshrined in attendance in the court of the Shizu temple.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin day in the intercalary tenth month of Mingchang 5, Huandu, Duke of Dai; Yehe, Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and Purple Ribbon; Hezhe, Special Advancement; Penna, Grand Master of the State with Unequalled Honor; and Bada, Grand Master of the State with Unequalled Honor were enshrined in attendance in the court of the Shizu temple.

sentences.zh: 天德二年二月，太廟祫享，有司擬上配享功臣，詔以撒改，辭不失、斜也杲、斡魯。

translations.literal: In the second month of the second year of Tiande, at the Grand Ancestral Temple's xia offering, the responsible officials proposed worthy officials to be enshrined in attendance; the edict named Sacai, Xibushi, Xieye Guo, and Wolu.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Tiande 2, at the Grand Ancestral Temple's xia offering, the responsible officials proposed worthy officials for enshrinement in attendance; the edict named Sacai, Xibushi, Xieye Guo, and Wolu.

sentences.zh: 阿思魁忠東向，配太祖位。

translations.literal: Asiqui Zhong faced east, enshrined in attendance with the seat of Taizu.
translations.idiomatic: Asiqui Zhong faced east, enshrined in attendance with Taizu's seat.

sentences.zh: 以粘哥宗翰、翰裏不宗望、闍母。

translations.literal: Niange Zonghan, Hanlibu Zongwang, and Zhanmu.
translations.idiomatic: Niange Zonghan, Hanlibu Zongwang, and Zhanmu.

sentences.zh: 婁室、銀朮可西向，配太宗位。

translations.literal: Loushi and Yinshu Ke faced west, enshrined in attendance with the seat of Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Loushi and Yinshu Ke faced west, enshrined in attendance with Taizong's seat.

sentences.zh: 大定三年十月，祫享，又以斜也、斡魯、撒改、習不失、阿思魁配享太祖，宗望、闍母、宗翰、婁室、銀朮哥配享太宗。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the third year of Dading, at the xia offering, Xieye, Wolu, Sacai, Xibushi, and Asiqui were again enshrined in attendance with Taizu; Zongwang, Zhanmu, Zonghan, Loushi, and Yinshu Ge were enshrined in attendance with Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of Dading 3, at the xia offering, Xieye, Wolu, Sacai, Xibushi, and Asiqui were again enshrined in attendance with Taizu, while Zongwang, Zhanmu, Zonghan, Loushi, and Yinshu Ge were enshrined in attendance with Taizong.

sentences.zh: 其後，次序屢有更易。

translations.literal: Thereafter the order was changed repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the order was changed repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 八年，上命圖畫功臣于太祖廟，有司第祖宗佐命之臣，勳績之大小、官資之崇卑以次上聞。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, the emperor ordered portraits of worthy officials painted in the Taizu temple; the responsible officials ranked the ministers who had aided the founding ancestors, reporting them in order according to the magnitude of their achievements and the eminence of their offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, the emperor ordered portraits of worthy officials painted in the Taizu temple. The responsible officials ranked the ministers who had aided the founding ancestors and reported them in order according to the magnitude of their achievements and the eminence of their offices.

sentences.zh: 乃定左廡：開府金源郡王撒改、皇伯太師右副元帥宋王宗望、開府金源郡王斡魯、皇伯太師粱王宗弼、開府金源郡王婁室、皇叔祖元帥左都監魯王闍母、開府隋國公阿離合懣、儀同三司袞國公劉彥宗、右丞相齊國簡懿公韓企先、特進宗人習失；

translations.literal: The left wing was then fixed as follows: Sacai, Prince of Jinyuan Commandery and Grand Master of the State with Unequalled Honor; Zongwang, Prince of Song, Imperial Uncle, Grand Preceptor, and Vice Commander-in-Chief of the Right; Wolu, Prince of Jinyuan Commandery and Grand Master of the State with Unequalled Honor; Zongbi, Prince of Liang, Imperial Uncle and Grand Preceptor; Loushi, Prince of Jinyuan Commandery and Grand Master of the State with Unequalled Honor; Zhanmu, Prince of Lu, Imperial Great-Uncle, Commander-in-Chief, and Left Chief Overseer; Alihemen, Duke of Sui and Grand Master of the State with Unequalled Honor; Liu Yanzong, Duke of Gun and Grand Master of the State with Unequalled Honor; Han Qixian, Duke of Qi, Right Chancellor, and Lord of Jianyi; and Xishi, Special Advancement and clansman;
translations.idiomatic: The left wing was then fixed as follows: Sacai, Prince of Jinyuan Commandery; Zongwang, Prince of Song, Imperial Uncle, Grand Preceptor, and Vice Commander-in-Chief of the Right; Wolu, Prince of Jinyuan Commandery; Zongbi, Prince of Liang, Imperial Uncle and Grand Preceptor; Loushi, Prince of Jinyuan Commandery; Zhanmu, Prince of Lu, Imperial Great-Uncle, Commander-in-Chief, and Left Chief Overseer; Alihemen, Duke of Sui; Liu Yanzong, Duke of Gun; Han Qixian, Duke of Qi and Right Chancellor; and Xishi, Special Advancement and clansman;

sentences.zh: 右廡：太師秦王宗翰、皇叔祖遼王杲、開府金源郡王習不失、開府金源郡王完顏希尹、太傅楚王宗雄、開府前燕京留守金源郡王完顏銀朮哥、開府金源郡王完顏忠、金源郡王完顏撒離喝、特進宗人斡魯古、右丞相金源郡王紇石烈志寧。

translations.literal: The right wing: Zonghan, Prince of Qin and Grand Preceptor; Guo, Prince of Liao and Imperial Great-Uncle; Xibushi, Prince of Jinyuan Commandery and Grand Master of the State with Unequalled Honor; Wanyan Xiyin, Prince of Jinyuan Commandery and Grand Master of the State with Unequalled Honor; Zongxiong, Prince of Chu and Grand Tutor; Wanyan Yinshu Ge, Prince of Jinyuan Commandery, former Metropolitan Prefect of Yanjing, and Grand Master of the State with Unequalled Honor; Wanyan Zhong, Prince of Jinyuan Commandery and Grand Master of the State with Unequalled Honor; Wanyan Salihua, Prince of Jinyuan Commandery; Wolugu, Special Advancement and clansman; and He Shilie Zhining, Prince of Jinyuan Commandery and Right Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The right wing: Zonghan, Prince of Qin and Grand Preceptor; Guo, Prince of Liao and Imperial Great-Uncle; Xibushi, Prince of Jinyuan Commandery; Wanyan Xiyin, Prince of Jinyuan Commandery; Zongxiong, Prince of Chu and Grand Tutor; Wanyan Yinshu Ge, Prince of Jinyuan Commandery and former Metropolitan Prefect of Yanjing; Wanyan Zhong, Prince of Jinyuan Commandery; Wanyan Salihua, Prince of Jinyuan Commandery; Wolugu, Special Advancement and clansman; and He Shilie Zhining, Prince of Jinyuan Commandery and Right Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 十六年，左廡遷粱王宗弼于斡魯上。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year, on the left wing Prince Zongbi of Liang was moved above Wolu.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year, on the left wing Prince Zongbi of Liang was moved above Wolu.

sentences.zh: 十八年，黜習失，而次蒲家奴于阿離合懣下。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, Xishi was removed, and Pujianu was placed next below Alihemen.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year, Xishi was removed and Pujianu was placed next below Alihemen.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，增皇伯太師遼王，斜也、撒改、宗幹、宗翰、宗望，其下以次列。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year, the Imperial Uncle, Grand Preceptor, and Prince of Liao were added, along with Xieye, Sacai, Zonggan, Zonghan, and Zongwang, with those below listed in order beneath them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year, the Imperial Uncle, Grand Preceptor, and Prince of Liao were added, along with Xieye, Sacai, Zonggan, Zonghan, and Zongwang, with those below listed in order beneath them.

sentences.zh: 至明昌四年，次序始定。

translations.literal: By the fourth year of Mingchang the order was finally fixed.
translations.idiomatic: By Mingchang 4 the order was finally fixed.

sentences.zh: 東廊：皇叔祖遼智烈王斜也杲、皇伯太師遼忠烈王宗幹斡本、皇伯太師右副元帥宋桓肅王訛魯補宗望、開府儀同三司金源郡毅武王習不失、開府儀同三司金源郡貞憲王顏谷神希尹、太傅楚威敏王謀良虎宗雄、開府儀同三司燕京留守金源郡襄武王完顏銀朮可、開府儀同三司金源郡明毅王完顏忠阿思魁、金源郡莊襄王杲撒離喝、特進宗人斡裏古莊翼，特進完顏習失威敬、太師尚書令淄忠烈王徒單克甯、太師尚書令南陽郡文康王張浩。

sentences.zh: 西廊：開府儀同三司金源郡忠毅王撒改、太師秦桓忠王粘罕宗翰、皇伯太師粱忠烈王斡出宗弼、開府儀同三司金源郡剛烈王斡魯、開府儀同三司金源郡莊義王完顏婁室、皇叔祖元師左都監魯莊明王闍母、開府儀同三司隋國剛憲公阿離合懣、開府儀同三司豫國襄毅公蒲家奴昱、開府儀同三司袞國英敏公劉彥宗、右丞相齊國簡懿公韓企先、太保尚書令廣平郡襄簡王李石、開府儀同三司右丞相金源郡武定王紇石烈志寧、開府儀同三司左丞相沂國公僕散忠義、儀同三司左丞相崇國公紇石烈良弼、右丞相莘國公石琚、右丞相申國公唐括安禮、開府儀同三司平章政事徒單合喜、參知政事宗敘。

sentences.zh: 每一朝為一列，著為令。

translations.literal: Each reign formed one row, and this was established as a statute.
translations.idiomatic: Each reign formed one row, and this was established as a statute.

sentences.zh: 凡天子大祀，則陳八寶及勝國寶於庭，所以示守也。

translations.literal: Whenever the Son of Heaven performed a great sacrifice, the Eight Treasures and the seals of conquered states were displayed in the courtyard, thereby showing what the dynasty held in custody.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Son of Heaven performed a great sacrifice, the Eight Treasures and the seals of conquered states were displayed in the courtyard to show what the dynasty held in custody.

sentences.zh: 金克遼、宋所得寶玉，及本朝所制，今並載焉。

translations.literal: The jade and treasure seals taken when Jin conquered Liao and Song, together with those made by the present dynasty, are all recorded here.
translations.idiomatic: The jade and treasure seals taken when Jin conquered Liao and Song, together with those made by the present dynasty, are all recorded here.

sentences.zh: 獲於遼者，玉寶四、金寶二。

translations.literal: Taken from Liao: four jade seals and two gold seals.
translations.idiomatic: Taken from Liao: four jade seals and two gold seals.

sentences.zh: 玉寶：「通天萬歲之璽」一，「受天明命惟德乃昌」之寶一皆方三寸，「嗣聖」寶一，禦封不辨印文寶一。

translations.literal: Jade seals: one "Seal of Penetrating Heaven and Ten Thousand Years," one "Treasure of Receiving Heaven's Bright Mandate—Only Virtue Brings Prosperity," both square and three inches; one "Heir to the Sage" seal; and one imperial seal whose inscription could not be deciphered.
translations.idiomatic: Jade seals: one "Seal of Penetrating Heaven and Ten Thousand Years," one "Treasure of Receiving Heaven's Bright Mandate—Only Virtue Brings Prosperity," both square and three inches; one "Heir to the Sage" seal; and one imperial seal whose inscription could not be deciphered.

sentences.zh: 金寶：「御前之寶」一，「書詔之寶」一，二寶金初用之。

translations.literal: Gold seals: one "Treasure Before the Throne" and one "Treasure of Written Edicts"; these two seals were used at the beginning of the Jin dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Gold seals: one "Treasure Before the Throne" and one "Treasure of Written Edicts"; these two seals were used at the beginning of the Jin dynasty.

sentences.zh: 獲于宋者，玉寶十五，金寶七、印一，金塗銀寶五。

translations.literal: Taken from Song: fifteen jade seals, seven gold seals and one stamp, and five gold-plated silver seals.
translations.idiomatic: Taken from Song: fifteen jade seals, seven gold seals and one stamp, and five gold-plated silver seals.

sentences.zh: 玉寶：受命寶一，咸陽所得，三寸六分，文曰「受命於天，既壽永昌」，相傳為秦璽，白玉蓋，螭紐。

translations.literal: Jade seals: one Mandate-receiving seal, obtained at Xianyang, three inches and six tenths, inscribed "Having received the mandate from Heaven, may you long enjoy enduring prosperity"; traditionally said to be the Qin imperial seal, with a white jade cap and a chi-dragon knob.
translations.idiomatic: Jade seals: one Mandate-receiving seal, obtained at Xianyang, three inches and six tenths, inscribed "Having received the mandate from Heaven, may you long enjoy enduring prosperity"—traditionally said to be the Qin imperial seal, the Heirloom Seal of the Realm, with a white jade cap and a chi-dragon knob.

sentences.zh: 傳國寶一，螭紐。

translations.literal: One seal of transmission of the realm, with a chi-dragon knob.
translations.idiomatic: One seal of transmission of the realm, with a chi-dragon knob.

sentences.zh: 鎮國寶一，二面並碧色，文曰「承天休，延萬億，永無極」。

translations.literal: One seal of stabilizing the realm, both faces green, inscribed "Receiving Heaven's favor, extending ten thousand myriads, forever without limit."
translations.idiomatic: One seal of stabilizing the realm, both faces green, inscribed "Receiving Heaven's favor, extending ten thousand myriads, forever without limit."

sentences.zh: 又受命寶一，文曰「受命於天，既壽永昌」。

translations.literal: Another Mandate-receiving seal, inscribed "Having received the mandate from Heaven, may you long enjoy enduring prosperity."
translations.idiomatic: Another Mandate-receiving seal, inscribed "Having received the mandate from Heaven, may you long enjoy enduring prosperity."

translations.idiomatic: One "Treasure of the Son of Heaven."

translations.idiomatic: One "Credential Seal of the Son of Heaven."

translations.idiomatic: One "Travelling Seal of the Son of Heaven."

translations.idiomatic: One "Seal of the Emperor."

translations.idiomatic: One "Travelling Seal of the Emperor."

translations.literal: Two "Treasures of the Emperor Reverently Receiving Heaven's Mandate."
translations.idiomatic: Two "Treasures of the Emperor Reverently Receiving Heaven's Mandate."

sentences.zh: 皆四寸八分，螭紐。

translations.literal: All were four inches and eight tenths, with chi-dragon knobs.
translations.idiomatic: All were four inches and eight tenths, with chi-dragon knobs.

sentences.zh: 「禦書之寶」二，一龍紐，一螭紐。

translations.literal: Two "Treasures of Imperial Writing," one with a dragon knob and one with a chi-dragon knob.
translations.idiomatic: Two "Treasures of Imperial Writing," one with a dragon knob and one with a chi-dragon knob.

translations.literal: One "Treasure of the Xuanhe Imperial Brush," with a chi-dragon knob.
translations.idiomatic: One "Treasure of the Xuanhe Imperial Brush," with a chi-dragon knob.

sentences.zh: 金寶並印：「天下同文之寶」一，龍紐。

translations.literal: Gold seals and stamps: one "Treasure of Universal Script Under Heaven," with a dragon knob.
translations.idiomatic: Gold seals and stamps: one "Treasure of Universal Script Under Heaven," with a dragon knob.

sentences.zh: 「御前之寶」二。

translations.literal: Two "Treasures Before the Throne."
translations.idiomatic: Two "Treasures Before the Throne."

translations.literal: One "Treasure of Imperial Writing."
translations.idiomatic: One "Treasure of Imperial Writing."

translations.literal: One "Treasure of the Xuanhe Hall."
translations.idiomatic: One "Treasure of the Xuanhe Hall."

translations.literal: One "Seal of the Empress."
translations.idiomatic: One "Seal of the Empress."

translations.literal: One "Seal of the Crown Prince," with a tortoise knob.
translations.idiomatic: One "Seal of the Crown Prince," with a tortoise knob.

sentences.zh: 「皇太子妃」印一，龜紐。

translations.literal: One seal of the "Crown Prince's Consort," with a tortoise knob.
translations.idiomatic: One seal of the "Crown Prince's Consort," with a tortoise knob.

sentences.zh: 金塗銀寶：「皇帝欽崇國祀之寶」一，「天下合同之寶」一，「御前之寶」一，「御前錫賜之寶」一，「書詔之寶」一。

translations.literal: Gold-plated silver seals: one "Treasure of the Emperor Reverently Honoring the State's Sacrifices," one "Treasure of Universal Concord Under Heaven," one "Treasure Before the Throne," one "Treasure of Imperial Bestowal Before the Throne," and one "Treasure of Written Edicts."
translations.idiomatic: Gold-plated silver seals: one "Treasure of the Emperor Reverently Honoring the State's Sacrifices," one "Treasure of Universal Concord Under Heaven," one "Treasure Before the Throne," one "Treasure of Imperial Bestowal Before the Throne," and one "Treasure of Written Edicts."

sentences.zh: 外有宋內府圖書印三十八。

translations.literal: Besides these there were thirty-eight Song Inner Repository library seals.
translations.idiomatic: Besides these there were thirty-eight Song Inner Repository library seals.

sentences.zh: 「內府圖書之印」一、「禦書」三、「御筆」一、「禦畫」一，「禦書玉寶」一、「天子萬年」一、「天子萬壽」一、「龜龍上珍」一、「河洛元瑞」二、「雲漢之章」一、「奎璧之文」一、「華國之瑞」一、「大觀中秘」一、「大觀寶篆」一、「政和」一、「宜和」三、「宜和禦覺」一、「宣和中秘」一、「宣和殿制」一、「宣和大寶」一、「宣和書寶」二、「宣和畫寶」一、「常樂未央」一、古文二、「封」四，共三十五面，並玉。

translations.literal: "Inner Repository Library Seal" one; "Imperial Writing" three; "Imperial Brush" one; "Imperial Painting" one; "Imperial Writing Jade Seal" one; "Ten Thousand Years of the Son of Heaven" one; "Ten Thousand Longevities of the Son of Heaven" one; "Supreme Treasures of Turtle and Dragon" one; "Primordial Omen of the Yellow River and Luo" two; "Chapter of Clouds and Milky Way" one; "Text of Kui and Bi" one; "Auspice of the Flourishing Realm" one; "Secret Archive of Daguang" one; "Treasured Seal Script of Daguang" one; "Zhenghe" one; "Yihe" three; "Yihe Imperial Reading" one; "Secret Archive of Xuanhe" one; "Made by the Xuanhe Hall" one; "Great Treasure of Xuanhe" one; "Writing Seal of Xuanhe" two; "Painting Seal of Xuanhe" one; "Everlasting Joy Without End" one; two in ancient script; four reading "Seal"; thirty-five faces in all, all of jade.

sentences.zh: 「封」字一、「禦畫」一，二面並馬瑙。

translations.literal: One reading "Seal" and one "Imperial Painting"—both faces of agate.
translations.idiomatic: One reading "Seal" and one "Imperial Painting"—both faces of agate.

sentences.zh: 「政和御筆」一，系水晶。

translations.literal: One "Zhenghe Imperial Brush," with crystal cord.
translations.idiomatic: One "Zhenghe Imperial Brush," with crystal cord.

sentences.zh: 玄圭一，白玉圭一十九。

translations.literal: One black jade tablet and nineteen white jade tablets.
translations.idiomatic: One black jade tablet and nineteen white jade tablets.

sentences.zh: 本朝所制。

translations.literal: Made by the present dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: Made by the present dynasty.

sentences.zh: 國初就用遼寶，皇統五年始鑄金「御前之寶」一、「書詔之寶」一。

translations.literal: At the founding of the state the dynasty at first used the Liao seals; in the fifth year of Huangtong it first cast gold seals: one "Treasure Before the Throne" and one "Treasure of Written Edicts."
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the state the dynasty at first used the Liao seals; in Huangtong 5 it first cast gold seals: one "Treasure Before the Throne" and one "Treasure of Written Edicts."

sentences.zh: 大定十八年，得美玉，詔作「大金受命萬世之寶」，其制徑四寸八分，厚寸四分，盤龍紐高厚各四寸六分。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Dading, fine jade was obtained, and an edict ordered the making of the "Great Jin Treasure of Receiving the Mandate for Ten Thousand Generations"; it measured four inches and eight tenths in diameter, one inch and four tenths thick, with a coiled-dragon knob four inches and six tenths in height and thickness.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 18, fine jade was obtained, and an edict ordered the making of the "Great Jin Treasure of Receiving the Mandate for Ten Thousand Generations"; it measured four inches and eight tenths in diameter, one inch and four tenths thick, with a coiled-dragon knob four inches and six tenths in height and thickness.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，又鑄「宣命之寶」，其徑四寸二厘，厚一寸四分，紐高一寸九分，字深二分。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, the "Treasure of Proclaimed Commands" was cast as well; its diameter was four inches and two hao, its thickness one inch and four tenths, the knob one inch and nine tenths high, and the characters two tenths deep.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, the "Treasure of Proclaimed Commands" was cast as well; its diameter was four inches and two hao, its thickness one inch and four tenths, the knob one inch and nine tenths high, and the characters two tenths deep.

sentences.zh: 敕有司議所當用，奏：「今所收八寶及皇統五年造'御前之寶'，賜宋國書及常例奏目則用之，'書詔之寶'，賜高麗、夏國詔並頒詔則用之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the responsible officials to discuss which seals should be used; they memorialized: "The Eight Treasures now collected and the 'Treasure Before the Throne' made in Huangtong 5 are to be used when bestowing letters on the Song state and for routine memorial registers; the 'Treasure of Written Edicts' is to be used when bestowing edicts on Goryeo and Western Xia and when promulgating edicts generally.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered the responsible officials to discuss which seals should be used; they reported: "The Eight Treasures now collected and the 'Treasure Before the Throne' made in Huangtong 5 are to be used when bestowing letters on the Song state and for routine memorial registers; the 'Treasure of Written Edicts' is to be used when bestowing edicts on Goryeo and Western Xia and when promulgating edicts generally.

sentences.zh: 大定十八年造'大金受命萬世之寶'，奉敕再議。

translations.literal: The 'Great Jin Treasure of Receiving the Mandate for Ten Thousand Generations' made in Dading 18 was, by imperial command, discussed again.
translations.idiomatic: The "Great Jin Treasure of Receiving the Mandate for Ten Thousand Generations" made in Dading 18 was, by imperial command, discussed again.

sentences.zh: 今所鑄金寶宜以進呈為始，一品及王公妃用玉寶，二品以下用金'宣命之寶'。

translations.literal: The gold seals now cast should begin with presentation to the throne: those of the first rank and princes' consorts use jade seals, and those of the second rank and below use the gold 'Treasure of Proclaimed Commands.'
translations.idiomatic: The gold seals now cast should begin with presentation to the throne: those of the first rank and princes' consorts use jade seals, and those of the second rank and below use the gold "Treasure of Proclaimed Commands."

sentences.zh: 」又有「禮信之寶」，用銅，歲賜三國禮物緘封用之，明昌間更以銀。

translations.literal: There was also the "Treasure of Ritual Credence," made of copper, used to seal the annual gifts to the three states; during the Mingchang period it was changed to silver.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the "Treasure of Ritual Credence," made of copper, used to seal the annual gifts to the three states; during the Mingchang period it was changed to silver.

sentences.zh: 又有太皇太后、皇太后、皇后、皇太妃寶，又有皇太子及守國寶，皆用金。

translations.literal: There were also seals of the Grand Empress Dowager, Empress Dowager, Empress, and Imperial Consort Dowager, and there were also the crown prince's seal and the regency seal—all of gold.
translations.idiomatic: There were also seals of the Grand Empress Dowager, Empress Dowager, Empress, and Imperial Consort Dowager, and there were also the crown prince's seal and the regency seal—all of gold.

sentences.zh: 大定二十四年，皇太子寶，金鑄龜紐，有司定其文曰「監國」，上命以「守」易「監」，比親王印廣長各加一分。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year of Dading, the crown prince's seal was cast in gold with a tortoise knob; the responsible officials fixed its inscription as "Regent of the State," but the emperor ordered "Guardian" substituted for "Regent," and compared with princes' seals its width and length were each increased by one tenth.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 24, the crown prince's seal was cast in gold with a tortoise knob; the responsible officials fixed its inscription as "Regent of the State," but the emperor ordered "Guardian" substituted for "Regent," and compared with princes' seals its width and length were each increased by one tenth.

sentences.zh: 大定三年八月，有司議：「祫享犧牲品物，按唐《開元禮》宋《開寶禮》每室犢一、羊一、豬一，《五禮新儀》每室複加魚十有五尾。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the third year of Dading, the responsible officials discussed: "For the sacrificial offerings at the xia offering, according to Tang's Kaiyuan Li and Song's Kaibao Li, each chamber used one calf, one sheep, and one pig; the Five Rites New Protocols added fifteen fish per chamber as well.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of Dading 3, the responsible officials discussed: "For the sacrificial offerings at the xia offering, according to Tang's Kaiyuan Li and Song's Kaibao Li, each chamber used one calf, one sheep, and one pig; the Five Rites New Protocols added fifteen fish per chamber as well.

sentences.zh: 天德、貞元例，與唐、宋同，有司行事則不用太牢，七祀功臣羊各二，酒共二百一十瓶。

translations.literal: The precedents of Tiande and Zhenyuan followed Tang and Song; when officials performed the rite the full sacrificial set was not used; for the seven shrines and worthy officials, each had two sheep, with two hundred and ten bottles of wine in total.
translations.idiomatic: The precedents of Tiande and Zhenyuan followed Tang and Song; when officials performed the rite the full sacrificial set was not used; for the seven shrines and worthy officials, each had two sheep, with two hundred and ten bottles of wine in total.

sentences.zh: 正降減定，通用犢一，兩室共用羊一豕一，酒百瓶，此于禮有闕。

translations.literal: Under the reduced standards of the Zhengjiang period, one calf was used for all, two chambers shared one sheep and one pig, and wine was one hundred bottles—this was deficient in ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: Under the reduced standards of the Zhengjiang period, one calf was used for all, two chambers shared one sheep and one pig, and wine was one hundred bottles—this was deficient in ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 今七祀功臣牲酒請依天德制，宗廟每室則用宋制，加魚。

translations.literal: We request that the livestock and wine for the seven shrines and worthy officials follow the Tiande regulations, while for each chamber of the ancestral temple Song's standard should be used, with fish added.
translations.idiomatic: We request that the livestock and wine for the seven shrines and worthy officials follow the Tiande regulations, while for each chamber of the ancestral temple Song's standard should be used, with fish added.

sentences.zh: 然每室一犢恐太豐。

translations.literal: Yet one calf per chamber may prove overly lavish.
translations.idiomatic: Yet one calf per chamber may prove overly lavish.

sentences.zh: 」世宗乃命每祭共用一犢，羊豕如舊。

translations.literal: The Shizu emperor then ordered that each sacrifice use one shared calf, with sheep and pigs as before.
translations.idiomatic: The Shizu emperor then ordered that each sacrifice use one shared calf, with sheep and pigs as before.

sentences.zh: 又以九月五日祫享，當用鹿肉五十斤、麞肉三十五斤、兔十四頭為臡醢，以貞元、正降時方禁獵，皆以羊代，此禮殊為未備，詔從古制。

translations.literal: Moreover, the xia offering on the fifth day of the ninth month should use fifty jin of venison, thirty-five jin of roe-deer meat, and fourteen hares for minced-and-pickled offerings; during Zhenyuan and Zhengjiang hunting had been prohibited, so sheep were substituted—the rite was quite incomplete, and an edict ordered a return to the ancient standard.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the xia offering on the fifth day of the ninth month should use fifty jin of venison, thirty-five jin of roe-deer meat, and fourteen hares for minced-and-pickled offerings; during Zhenyuan and Zhengjiang hunting had been prohibited, so sheep were substituted—the rite was quite incomplete, and an edict ordered a return to the ancient standard.

sentences.zh: 十年正月，詔宰臣曰：「古禮殺牛以祭，後世有更者否？

translations.literal: In the first month of the tenth year, an edict to the chief ministers said: "Ancient ritual slaughters cattle for sacrifice—have later ages changed this?
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the tenth year, an edict to the chief ministers said: "Ancient ritual slaughters cattle for sacrifice—have later ages changed this?

sentences.zh: 其檢討典故以聞。

translations.literal: Examine the precedents and report.
translations.idiomatic: Examine the precedents and report.

sentences.zh: 」有司謂：「自周以來，下逮唐、宋，祫享無不用牛者。

translations.literal: The responsible officials said: "From Zhou down through Tang and Song, the xia offering never failed to use cattle.
translations.idiomatic: The responsible officials said: "From Zhou down through Tang and Song, the xia offering never failed to use cattle.

sentences.zh: 唐《開元禮》時享每室各用太牢一，至天寶六年始減牛數，太廟每享用一犢。

translations.literal: Tang's Kaiyuan Li prescribed one full sacrificial set for each chamber at seasonal offerings; only in the sixth year of Tianbao was the number of cattle reduced, and the Grand Ancestral Temple used one calf per seasonal offering.
translations.idiomatic: Tang's Kaiyuan Li prescribed one full sacrificial set for each chamber at seasonal offerings; only in Tianbao 6 was the number of cattle reduced, and the Grand Ancestral Temple used one calf per seasonal offering.

sentences.zh: 宋《政和五禮新儀》時享太廟，親祀用牛，有司行事則不用。

translations.literal: Song's Zhenghe Five Rites New Protocols for seasonal offerings at the Grand Ancestral Temple used cattle when the emperor sacrificed in person, but not when officials performed the rite.
translations.idiomatic: Song's Zhenghe Five Rites New Protocols for seasonal offerings at the Grand Ancestral Temple used cattle when the emperor sacrificed in person, but not when officials performed the rite.

sentences.zh: 宋開寶二年詔，昊天上帝、皇地祇用犢，餘大祀皆以羊豕代之。

translations.literal: An edict of the second year of Kaibao in Song ordered that the Grand Exalted Deity of Heaven and Imperial Earth use a calf, while all other major sacrifices substitute sheep and pigs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict of Kaibao 2 in Song ordered that the Grand Exalted Deity of Heaven and Imperial Earth use a calf, while all other major sacrifices substitute sheep and pigs.

sentences.zh: 合二羊五豕足代一犢。

translations.literal: Two sheep and five pigs together suffice to replace one calf.
translations.idiomatic: Two sheep and five pigs together suffice to replace one calf.

sentences.zh: 今三年一祫乃為親祠，其禮至重，每室一犢後恐難省減。

translations.literal: The triennial xia offering is a personal sacrifice by the emperor, and the rite is of the utmost weight—one calf per chamber would be hard to reduce later.
translations.idiomatic: The triennial xia offering is a personal sacrifice by the emperor, and the rite is of the utmost weight—one calf per chamber would be hard to reduce later.

sentences.zh: 」遂命時享與祭社稷如舊，若親祠宗廟則共用一犢，有司行事則不用。

translations.literal: It was therefore ordered that seasonal offerings and sacrifices to the altars of soil and grain follow the old practice; if the emperor sacrificed in person at the ancestral temple, one shared calf was used, but not when officials performed the rite.
translations.idiomatic: It was therefore ordered that seasonal offerings and sacrifices to the altars of soil and grain follow the old practice; if the emperor sacrificed in person at the ancestral temple, one shared calf was used, but not when officials performed the rite.

sentences.zh: 十二年十月，祫享，以攝官行事，詔共用三犢。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the twelfth year, at the xia offering with an acting official performing the rite, an edict ordered three shared calves.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the twelfth year, at the xia offering with an acting official performing the rite, an edict ordered three shared calves.

sentences.zh: 二十二年十月，詔祫禘共用三犢，有司行事則以鹿代。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the twenty-second year, an edict ordered that xia and di offerings share three calves; when officials performed the rite, deer were substituted.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the twenty-second year, an edict ordered that xia and di offerings share three calves; when officials performed the rite, deer were substituted.

sentences.zh: 昭德皇后廟大定十九年禘祭，不用犢。

translations.literal: At Empress Zhaode's temple, the di offering in Dading 19 used no calf.
translations.idiomatic: At Empress Zhaode's temple, the di offering in Dading 19 used no calf.

sentences.zh: 大定二十九年，章宗即位，禮官言：「自大定二十七年十月袷享，至今年正月世宗升遐，故四月不行禘禮。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year of Dading, when Zhangzong ascended the throne, the ritual officials said: "From the xia offering in the tenth month of Dading 27 until the first month of this year, when Shizu passed away, the di rite was therefore not performed in the fourth month.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 29, when Zhangzong ascended the throne, the ritual officials said: "From the xia offering in the tenth month of Dading 27 until the first month of this year, when Shizu passed away, the di rite was therefore not performed in the fourth month.

sentences.zh: 按《公羊傳》，閔公二年'吉禘于莊公，言吉者未可以吉，謂未三年也'。

translations.literal: According to the Gongyang Commentary, in Min year 2, 'An auspicious di offering to Duke Zhuang—the word "auspicious" means it was not yet permissible to be auspicious, meaning the mourning had not reached three years.'
translations.idiomatic: According to the Gongyang Commentary, in Min year 2, "An auspicious di offering to Duke Zhuang—the word 'auspicious' means it was not yet permissible to be auspicious, meaning the mourning had not reached three years."

sentences.zh: 注：'謂禘祫從先君數，朝聘從今君數，三年喪畢，遇禘則禘，遇祫則祫。

translations.literal: The annotation says: 'This means di and xia offerings are counted from the former lord, while court visits and tribute missions are counted from the present lord; once the three years of mourning are complete, when di comes, perform di; when xia comes, perform xia.
translations.idiomatic: The annotation says: "This means di and xia offerings are counted from the former lord, while court visits and tribute missions are counted from the present lord; once the three years of mourning are complete, when di comes, perform di; when xia comes, perform xia.

sentences.zh: '故事，宜於辛亥歲為大祥，三月禫祭，逾月則吉，則四月一日為初吉，適當孟夏禘祭之時，可為親祠。

translations.literal: 'By precedent, the great felicity should fall in the xinhai year, the end-of-mourning sacrifice in the third month, and after a month it is auspicious; thus the first day of the fourth month would be the initial auspicious day, coinciding with the midsummer di sacrifice—this could be a personal sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, the great felicity should fall in the xinhai year, the end-of-mourning sacrifice in the third month, and after a month it is auspicious; thus the first day of the fourth month would be the initial auspicious day, coinciding with the midsummer di sacrifice—this could be a personal sacrifice."

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: An edict approved it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved it.

sentences.zh: 及期，以孝懿皇后崩而止。

translations.literal: When the time came, it was halted because Empress Xiaoyi passed away.
translations.idiomatic: When the time came, it was halted because Empress Xiaoyi passed away.

sentences.zh: 五月，禮官言：「世宗升祔已三年，尚未合食於祖宗，若來冬遂行祫禮，伏為皇帝見居心喪，喪中之吉《春秋》譏其速，恐冬祫未可行。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, the ritual officials said: "Three years have passed since Shizu's enshrinement, yet he has not yet been united in sacrifice with the ancestors; if the xia rite is hurriedly performed next winter, I respectfully submit that the emperor is now in inner mourning—The Spring and Autumn Annals censure auspicious rites during mourning as too hasty—and I fear the winter xia cannot be performed.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, the ritual officials said: "Three years have passed since Shizu's enshrinement, yet he has not yet been united in sacrifice with the ancestors; if the xia rite is hurriedly performed next winter, I respectfully submit that the emperor is now in inner mourning—The Spring and Autumn Annals censure auspicious rites during mourning as too hasty—and I fear the winter xia cannot be performed.

sentences.zh: 然《周禮》王有哀慘則春官攝事，竊以世宗及孝懿皇后升祔以來，未曾躬謁，豈可令有司先攝事哉！

translations.literal: Yet the Rites of Zhou provide that when the king is in grief the Spring Office performs affairs by proxy; I take it that since Shizu and Empress Xiaoyi were enshrined, the emperor has never personally attended—how can officials be allowed to perform affairs by proxy first!
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Rites of Zhou provide that when the king is in grief the Spring Office performs affairs by proxy; I take it that since Shizu and Empress Xiaoyi were enshrined, the emperor has never personally attended—how can officials be allowed to perform affairs by proxy first!

sentences.zh: 況前代攝事者止施于常祀，今乞依故事，三年喪畢，祫則祫，禘則禘，於明昌四年四月一日釋心喪，行禘禮」。

translations.literal: Moreover, in former ages proxy performance was applied only to routine sacrifices; we now beg to follow precedent: when the three years of mourning are complete, perform xia when xia comes and di when di comes; on the first day of the fourth month of Mingchang 4 release inner mourning and perform the di rite."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in former ages proxy performance was applied only to routine sacrifices; we now beg to follow precedent: when the three years of mourning are complete, perform xia when xia comes and di when di comes; on the first day of the fourth month of Mingchang 4 release inner mourning and perform the di rite."

sentences.zh: 上從之。

translations.literal: The emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved it.

sentences.zh: 明昌三年十二月，尚書省奏：「明年親禘，室當用犢一。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of Mingchang 3, the Department of State memorialized: "For next year's personal di offering, each chamber should use one calf.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of Mingchang 3, the Department of State reported: "For next year's personal di offering, each chamber should use one calf.

sentences.zh: 欽懷皇后祔于明德之廟，按大定三年祫享，明德皇后室未嘗用犢。

translations.literal: Empress Qinhuai is enshrined in the temple of Mingde; according to the Dading 3 xia offering, Empress Mingde's chamber never used a calf.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Qinhuai is enshrined in the temple of Mingde; according to the Dading 3 xia offering, Empress Mingde's chamber never used a calf.

sentences.zh: 」敕欽懷皇后亦用之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that Empress Qinhuai also use one.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered that Empress Qinhuai also use one.

sentences.zh: 上因問拜數，右丞瑋具對，上曰：「世宗聖壽高，故殺其數，並不立於位，今當從禮而已。」

translations.literal: The emperor then asked about the number of bows; Right Vice Minister Wei answered in full, and the emperor said: "Shizu enjoyed great longevity, so the number was reduced and he did not stand at the positions; now we should simply follow the rites."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then asked about the number of bows; Right Vice Minister Wei answered in full, and the emperor said: "Shizu enjoyed great longevity, so the number was reduced and he did not stand at the positions; now we should simply follow the rites."

sentences.zh: 大定六年，定晨稞行禮，自大次至板位先見神之禮，兩拜。

translations.literal: In Dading 6, the morning grain-offering rite was fixed: from the grand side chamber to the spirit board position, the prior greeting of the spirits—two bows.
translations.idiomatic: In Dading 6, the morning grain-offering rite was fixed: from the grand side chamber to the spirit board position, the prior greeting of the spirits—two bows.

sentences.zh: 再至板位，又兩拜。

translations.literal: Returning to the spirit board position—two bows again.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to the spirit board position—two bows again.

sentences.zh: 稞鬯畢，還板位，再兩拜。

translations.literal: When the grain and aromatic spirits were finished, returning to the spirit board position—two bows again.
translations.idiomatic: When the grain and aromatic spirits were finished, returning to the spirit board position—two bows again.

sentences.zh: 還小次，酌獻時，罍洗位盥訖，至板位，先兩拜。

translations.literal: Returning to the minor side chamber; at the libation offering, after ablutions at the jar-washing position, reaching the spirit board position—two bows first.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to the minor side chamber; at the libation offering, after ablutions at the jar-washing position, reaching the spirit board position—two bows first.

sentences.zh: 酌獻畢還板位，再兩拜。

translations.literal: When the libation was finished, returning to the spirit board position—two bows again.
translations.idiomatic: When the libation was finished, returning to the spirit board position—two bows again.

sentences.zh: 止將始祖祝冊于板位西南安置，讀冊訖，又兩拜。

translations.literal: Only the founder ancestor's prayer text was placed southwest of the spirit board position; when the reading was finished—two bows again.
translations.idiomatic: Only the founder ancestor's prayer text was placed southwest of the spirit board position; when the reading was finished—two bows again.

sentences.zh: 還小次，又至飲福位，先兩拜，飲畢兩拜。

translations.literal: Returning to the minor side chamber, then going to the blessing-drinking position—two bows first, and when the drinking was finished—two bows.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to the minor side chamber, then going to the blessing-drinking position—two bows first, and when the drinking was finished—two bows.

sentences.zh: 凡十六拜。

translations.literal: Sixteen bows in all.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen bows in all.

sentences.zh: 貞祐四年，命參知政事李革為修奉太廟使，七月吉日親行祔享，有司以故事用皇帝時享儀，初至版位兩拜，晨稞及酌獻則每位三拜，飲福五拜，總七十九拜。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenyou, Vice Grand Councilor Li Ge was appointed commissioner for restoring and maintaining the Grand Ancestral Temple; on an auspicious day in the seventh month the emperor personally performed the enshrinement offering; the officials, following precedent, used the emperor's seasonal offering rite—two bows on first reaching the board position, three bows at each spirit for morning grain and libation offerings, five bows for blessing-drinking—seventy-nine bows in total.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenyou 4, Vice Grand Councilor Li Ge was appointed commissioner for restoring and maintaining the Grand Ancestral Temple; on an auspicious day in the seventh month the emperor personally performed the enshrinement offering; the officials, following precedent, used the emperor's seasonal offering rite—two bows on first reaching the board position, three bows at each spirit for morning grain and libation offerings, five bows for blessing-drinking—seventy-nine bows in total.

sentences.zh: 今升祔則遍及祧廟五室，則為一百九拜也。

translations.literal: Now enshrinement extends to all five chambers of the distant temple, making one hundred nine bows.
translations.idiomatic: Now enshrinement extends to all five chambers of the distant temple, making one hundred nine bows.

sentences.zh: 明昌間嘗減每位酌獻奠爵後一拜，則為九十二拜而已。

translations.literal: During Mingchang one bow after each libation offering and wine presentation per spirit was once reduced, leaving only ninety-two bows.
translations.idiomatic: During Mingchang one bow after each libation offering and wine presentation per spirit was once reduced, leaving only ninety-two bows.

sentences.zh: 然大定六年，世宗嘗令禮官通減為十六拜。

translations.literal: Yet in Dading 6, Shizu once ordered the ritual officials to reduce the total to sixteen bows.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in Dading 6, Shizu once ordered the ritual officials to reduce the total to sixteen bows.

sentences.zh: 又皇帝當散齋四日於別殿，致齋三日於大慶殿，今國事方殷，宜權散齋二日，致齋一日。

translations.literal: Moreover, the emperor should observe dispersed fasting for four days in a separate hall and concentrated fasting for three days in the Daqing Hall; as state affairs are now pressing, it is fitting provisionally to observe dispersed fasting for two days and concentrated fasting for one day.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the emperor should observe dispersed fasting for four days in a separate hall and concentrated fasting for three days in the Daqing Hall; as state affairs are now pressing, it is fitting provisionally to observe dispersed fasting for two days and concentrated fasting for one day.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「拜數從大定例，餘准奏。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The number of bows shall follow the Dading precedent; the rest is approved as memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The number of bows shall follow the Dading precedent; the rest is approved as reported.

sentences.zh: 」禮部尚書張行信言：「近奉詔從世宗十六拜之禮，臣與太常參定儀注，竊有疑焉。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Zhang Xingxin said: "Having recently received an edict to follow Shizu's sixteen-bow rite, your minister joined the Court of Imperial Sacrifices in fixing the protocol, and I have private doubts.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Rites Zhang Xingxin said: "Having recently received an edict to follow Shizu's sixteen-bow rite, your minister joined the Court of Imperial Sacrifices in fixing the protocol, and I have private doubts.

sentences.zh: 謹按唐、宋親祠典禮，皆有通拜及隨位拜禮。

translations.literal: I respectfully note that Tang and Song rites for personal sacrifice all include universal bows and position-by-position bows.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully note that Tang and Song rites for personal sacrifice all include universal bows and position-by-position bows.

sentences.zh: 世宗大定三年親行奉安之禮，亦通七拜，每室各五拜，合七十二拜。

translations.literal: When Shizu personally performed the enshrinement rite in Dading 3, there were seven universal bows and five bows at each chamber—seventy-two in all.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu personally performed the enshrinement rite in Dading 3, there were seven universal bows and five bows at each chamber—seventy-two in all.

sentences.zh: 逮六年禘，始敕有司減為十六拜，仍存七十二拜之儀，其意亦可見矣。

translations.literal: By the di offering of the sixth year, officials were first commanded to reduce it to sixteen bows, yet the seventy-two-bow rite was preserved—the intent is clear.
translations.idiomatic: By the di offering of the sixth year, officials were first commanded to reduce it to sixteen bows, yet the seventy-two-bow rite was preserved—the intent is clear.

sentences.zh: 蓋初年享禮以備，故後從權，更定通拜。

translations.literal: At first the seasonal offering rites were kept complete; afterward they were adjusted by expedient and universal bows were revised.
translations.idiomatic: At first the seasonal offering rites were kept complete; afterward they were adjusted by expedient and universal bows were revised.

sentences.zh: 今陛下初廟見奉安，而遽從此制，是於隨室神位並無拜禮，此臣之所疑一也；

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty's first temple visit for enshrinement would abruptly follow this regulation, meaning there are no bows at the spirit positions of each chamber—this is my first doubt;
translations.idiomatic: Now Your Majesty's first temple visit for enshrinement would abruptly follow this regulation, meaning there are no bows at the spirit positions of each chamber—this is my first doubt;

sentences.zh: 大定間十有二室，姑從十六拜，猶可。

translations.literal: During Dading there were twelve chambers—a provisional sixteen bows was still tolerable.
translations.idiomatic: During Dading there were twelve chambers—a provisional sixteen bows was still tolerable.

sentences.zh: 今十有七室。

translations.literal: Now there are seventeen chambers.
translations.idiomatic: Now there are seventeen chambers.

sentences.zh: 而拜數反不及之，此臣之所疑二也；

translations.literal: Yet the number of bows falls even below that—this is my second doubt;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the number of bows falls even below that—this is my second doubt;

sentences.zh: 況六年所定儀注，惟于皇帝板位前讀始祖一室祝冊。

translations.literal: Moreover, in the protocol fixed in the sixth year, only the founder ancestor's prayer text of one chamber was read before the emperor's spirit board position.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, in the protocol fixed in the sixth year, only the founder ancestor's prayer text of one chamber was read before the emperor's spirit board position.

sentences.zh: 夫祭有祝辭，本告神明，今諸祝冊各書帝后尊諡，及高曾祖考世次不一，皇帝所自稱亦自不同，而乃止讀一冊，餘皆虛設，恐于禮未安，此臣之所疑三也。

translations.literal: Sacrifices have prayer texts to address the spirits; now each prayer text records the posthumous titles of emperors and empresses, and the generations of great-great-grandfathers, grandfathers, and fathers differ, while the emperor's self-designations also differ—yet only one text is read and the rest are left empty; I fear this is not ritually sound—this is my third doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices have prayer texts to address the spirits; now each prayer text records the posthumous titles of emperors and empresses, and the generations of great-great-grandfathers, grandfathers, and fathers differ, while the emperor's self-designations also differ—yet only one text is read and the rest are left empty; I fear this is not ritually sound—this is my third doubt.

sentences.zh: 先王之禮順時施宜，不可多寡，惟稱而已。

translations.literal: The rites of former kings adapt to the times—neither too much nor too little, only what is fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The rites of former kings adapt to the times—neither too much nor too little, only what is fitting.

sentences.zh: 今近年禮官酌古今，別定四十四拜之禮。

translations.literal: Now in recent years the ritual officials, weighing ancient and modern practice, separately fixed a forty-four-bow rite.
translations.idiomatic: Now in recent years the ritual officials, weighing ancient and modern practice, separately fixed a forty-four-bow rite.

sentences.zh: 初見神二拜，晨稞通四拜，隨室酌獻讀祝畢兩拜，飲福四拜，似為得中。

translations.literal: Two bows on first greeting the spirits, four universal bows for morning grain, two bows after libation and prayer reading at each chamber, four bows for blessing-drinking—this seems a reasonable mean.
translations.idiomatic: Two bows on first greeting the spirits, four universal bows for morning grain, two bows after libation and prayer reading at each chamber, four bows for blessing-drinking—this seems a reasonable mean.

sentences.zh: 」上從之，乃定祔享如時享十二室之儀。

translations.literal: The emperor approved; the enshrinement offering was then fixed like the seasonal offering rite for twelve chambers.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved; the enshrinement offering was then fixed like the seasonal offering rite for twelve chambers.

sentences.zh: 又以祧廟五主始祖室不能容，止於室戶外東西一列，以西為上。

translations.literal: Because the five spirit tablets of the distant temple could not fit in the founder ancestor's chamber, they were placed in one row east and west outside the chamber doors, with the west as superior.
translations.idiomatic: Because the five spirit tablets of the distant temple could not fit in the founder ancestor's chamber, they were placed in one row east and west outside the chamber doors, with the west as superior.

sentences.zh: 神主闕者以升祔前三日廟內敬造，以享日醜前題寫畢，以次奉升。

translations.literal: Missing spirit tablets were reverently made within the temple three days before enshrinement; on the offering day, before the chou hour, inscriptions were completed and they were raised in order.
translations.idiomatic: Missing spirit tablets were reverently made within the temple three days before enshrinement; on the offering day, before the chou hour, inscriptions were completed and they were raised in order.

sentences.zh: 十月己未，親王百官自明俊殿奉迎祖宗神主於太廟幄次。

translations.literal: On the day jiwei in the tenth month, imperial princes and all officials escorted the spirit tablets of the ancestors from the Mingjun Hall to the tent-side quarters of the Grand Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On the day jiwei in the tenth month, imperial princes and all officials escorted the spirit tablets of the ancestors from the Mingjun Hall to the tent-side quarters of the Grand Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 辛酉行禮，用四十四拜之儀，無宮縣樂，犧牲從儉，十七室用犢三、羊豕九而已。

translations.literal: On xinyou they performed the rite using the forty-four-bow protocol, with no court music ensemble, sacrifices kept frugal—seventeen chambers using only three calves, nine sheep and pigs.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou they performed the rite using the forty-four-bow protocol, with no court music ensemble, sacrifices kept frugal—seventeen chambers using only three calves, nine sheep and pigs.

sentences.zh: 以皇太子為亞獻，濮王守純為終獻。

translations.literal: The crown prince served as secondary offerer, and Prince Pu Shouchun as final offerer.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince served as secondary offerer, and Prince Pu Shouchun as final offerer.

sentences.zh: 皇帝權服靴袍，行禮日服袞冕，皇太子以下公服，無鹵簿儀仗，禮畢乘馬還宮。

translations.literal: The emperor wore provisional dress of boots and robe; on the day of the rite he wore the dark ceremonial robe and cap; the crown prince and those below wore court dress; there was no guard of honor or ceremonial insignia; when the rite was finished they returned to the palace on horseback.
